feature: Home inline Copilot-readiness quiz — scoring / personalization correctness (result reflects the specific answers, distinct answers -> distinct results)
notes: Route/feature: artifacts/shane-mccaw-consulting/src/pages/Home.tsx — the inline 7-question
Copilot-readiness quiz in the hero (data-testid quiz-option-A..D per option, quiz-result on the
final result card). This manifest asserts the RESULT GENUINELY REFLECTS THE SPECIFIC ANSWERS,
not merely that 'a result appeared' — and drives >=2 distinct answer sets that must produce
genuinely DIFFERENT scores/bands, so a regression where personalization always returns the same
result regardless of input fails loudly here.
COMPLEMENTS, does not duplicate, copilot-readiness/money-path-e2e.json: that manifest clicks
quiz-option-A x7 only as the ENTRY navigation into the checkout money-path and asserts nothing
more than `expect quiz-result visible` (the exact 'some result appeared' gap this file closes).
This file's feature is the quiz SCORING itself, so it is a separate manifest per discover-before-create.
SCORING MODEL (verified against src/pages/home/quizData.ts + Home.tsx, NOT assumed):
VALUES = [0.18, 0.45, 0.7, 0.95] indexed by the chosen option (A/B/C/D).
wedges = the 6 PILLAR answers (Home.tsx answers[1..6]) mapped through VALUES (unanswered -> 0.1).
score  = Math.round( (sum(wedges) / 6) * 100 ).
band   = score>=80 'Advanced' | >=60 'Established' | >=40 'Developing' | else 'Early'.
QUESTIONS[0] is the CONTEXT/seat-count question (pillar -1); answers[0] sets the cohort phrase
ONLY and does NOT affect score. There are 7 questions total, so 7 clicks complete the quiz and
flip `done` true (the result card renders only when done).
All-A  -> every pillar 0.18 -> mean 0.18 -> score 18  -> band 'Early'.
All-C  -> every pillar 0.70 -> mean 0.70 -> score 70  -> band 'Established'.
All-D  -> every pillar 0.95 -> mean 0.95 -> score 95  -> band 'Advanced'.
Because a uniform option answers ALL 6 pillars, each expected score also depends on every pillar
contributing — so a dropped/ignored-pillar regression (a pillar stuck at the 0.1 default) shifts
the score off the asserted exact value and is caught here too.
HOW THE SPECIFIC SCORE IS ASSERTED (the load-bearing part): the framework's uiStep `expect` action
asserts element STATE ONLY (visible/hidden/present/absent — see UiTestExecutor.EvaluateExpectAsync);
it has no enforced DOM-text assertion. The score is dynamic text inside quiz-result with no
per-score testid, so this build adds scoped data-score={score} / data-band={band} attributes to the
quiz-result div in Home.tsx. That lets an ATTRIBUTE SELECTOR
([data-testid='quiz-result'][data-score='18'][data-band='Early']) assert the exact score+band via
genuine element presence — a wrong/unchanged result makes that selector NOT match and the step fails.
textContains CAVEAT (honest): Git #1016 added a uiSteps[].textContains field, but on the current
code it is ONLY plumbed loader -> AutomationAction (TestManifest.cs / MainWindow.xaml.cs:3738);
UiTestExecutor.EvaluateExpectAsync does NOT yet read it, so a textContains assertion is currently
SILENTLY NOT ENFORCED. It is therefore intentionally NOT used as coverage here — the data-score/
data-band attribute selector is the real assertion. (When #1016's executor wiring lands, a
textContains on the band word could be added as belt-and-suspenders.)
No apiTests/graphTests: the quiz is entirely client-side (no network call fires on completion; the
only quiz network call is the separate lead-capture form POST, out of scope for scoring). Each combo
re-navigates with `goto /` to reset React state (fresh mount: step 0, answers all null) — there is
no data-testid on the in-page 'Start over' button, and a fresh navigation is the cleanest reset.
